title: Docker in CI/CD
subtitle: Build, tag, and push Docker images to GHCR in GitHub Actions — with layer caching, multi-platform builds, and secure secrets

content.text: Build and push to GitHub Container Registry

content.code:
name: Build and Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']      # also build on version tags
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write   # required to push to GHCR

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Set up BuildKit (Docker's modern build engine — faster, more features)
      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      # Log in to GitHub Container Registry using GITHUB_TOKEN
      # No secret setup needed — GITHUB_TOKEN works automatically
      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Generate image tags:
      # - ghcr.io/owner/repo:main (branch name)
      # - ghcr.io/owner/repo:sha-abc1234 (commit SHA)
      # - ghcr.io/owner/repo:v1.2.3 (semver tag)
      # - ghcr.io/owner/repo:latest (only on tagged releases)
      - name: Extract metadata
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}
          tags: |
            type=ref,event=branch
            type=sha,prefix=sha-,format=short
            type=semver,pattern={{version}}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}}
            type=raw,value=latest,enable=${{ github.ref_type == 'tag' }}

      # Build and push with GitHub Actions cache
      - name: Build and push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          # Only push on main/tags, not on PR builds
          push: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          # GitHub Actions cache — reuse layers between runs
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

content.text: Without caching, every CI run downloads base images and reinstalls all dependencies from scratch — a Node.js app might take 3-4 minutes. With type=gha (GitHub Actions cache), BuildKit stores each Dockerfile layer after the first run. Subsequent runs that hit the cache take 30 seconds. The cache key is the layer content hash — if you change package.json, only the npm install layer and everything after it is rebuilt.

content.filename: Build for AMD64 and ARM64 simultaneously
content.code:
# Why: Apple Silicon Macs, AWS Graviton, Raspberry Pi all use ARM64
# Building multi-platform on GitHub's AMD64 runners uses QEMU emulation

- name: Set up QEMU
  uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3
  # QEMU allows running ARM64 code on AMD64 runners (slower but compatible)

- name: Set up Docker Buildx
  uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

- name: Build and push
  uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
  with:
    context: .
    platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
    push: true
    tags: ghcr.io/myorg/myapp:latest
    cache-from: type=gha
    cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
  # Creates a single image manifest that works on both architectures
  # docker pull ghcr.io/myorg/myapp:latest → gets the right architecture automatically

content.filename: BuildKit secrets — never in image layers
content.code:
- name: Build with secret
  uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
  with:
    context: .
    push: true
    tags: ghcr.io/myorg/myapp:latest
    secrets: |
      npm_token=${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
      github_token=${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    # In Dockerfile, use the secret without it being stored in layers:
    # RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npm_token \
    #     npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=$(cat /run/secrets/npm_token) && \
    #     npm ci && \
    #     npm config delete //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken

content.text: Don't push on pull request builds. The workflow uses push: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}. On PRs, the image is built and verified (you catch Dockerfile errors) but not pushed to the registry. This prevents untrusted code from PRs writing to your image registry, and avoids polluting the registry with thousands of PR build images.

questions.question: You use 'cache-from: type=gha, cache-to: type=gha,mode=max'. Your package.json changes. Which Dockerfile layers are rebuilt?
options: All layers — any file change invalidates the entire cache
Only the 'COPY package.json' layer and all layers after it (RUN npm ci, COPY src, etc.)
Only the final layer — Docker is smart enough to rebuild only what's needed
No layers — caching prevents any rebuilding
questions.explanation: Docker layer caching is sequential: each layer depends on all previous layers. When 'COPY package.json .' changes, that layer's cache is invalidated, and so is every layer that follows it (because they might depend on it). Layers before the COPY — like 'FROM node:20-alpine' and 'WORKDIR /app' — are still cached. This is why Dockerfile instruction order matters: 'COPY package.json → RUN npm ci → COPY src' is much faster to cache than 'COPY . → RUN npm ci'.

faq.q: Should I use Docker Hub or GHCR for my images?
faq.a: GHCR (ghcr.io) is the better default for GitHub-hosted projects: it's free, uses GITHUB_TOKEN (no separate secret setup), is colocated with your source code, and has no rate limits on pulls from GitHub Actions runners. Use Docker Hub if you need images accessible to non-GitHub users, or if you have existing infrastructure that already pulls from Docker Hub.

examples: The 'type=gha' build cache cut Docker build times from 4 minutes to 25 seconds for a Node.js API at a SaaS startup — just by adding two lines to the workflow

Multi-platform builds with QEMU are used by every major open source project (PostgreSQL, Redis, Node.js) to publish images that run on both Intel servers and ARM cloud instances without users needing to know the difference
